qs.q: What is the single most common cause of spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage in the general population?
qs.e: Ruptured saccular berry aneurysms are the most common cause of spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage, whereas trauma remains the most common cause of subarachnoid hemorrhage overall. Vascular malformations and tumors are less frequent causes.

qs.q: A 58-year-old woman dies suddenly from a subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by a ruptured berry aneurysm. Histological examination of the aneurysm neck typically reveals which structural alteration?
qs.e: Saccular aneurysms characteristically lack a media and the internal elastic lamina at the neck, representing the site of structural weakness. A normal arterial wall contains a robust media and elastic layers rather than total absence.

qs.q: What is the primary cause of spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH)?
qs.e: Rupture of a saccular aneurysm is the most common cause of spontaneous (non-traumatic) SAH. Trauma is the most common cause of SAH overall but is not spontaneous.

qs.q: A patient who suffered a severe subarachnoid hemorrhage following head trauma later develops progressive gait ataxia, urinary incontinence, and cognitive decline. What is the most likely mechanism of this sequela?
o: Obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid resorption in the subarachnoid space
Accumulation of tau-containing neurofibrillary tangles in frontal gyri
Recurrent bleeding from thin-walled subdural granulation vessels
Direct mechanical transection of the upper cervical spinal cord
qs.e: Posttraumatic hydrocephalus occurs due to the obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid resorption from subarachnoid hemorrhage. It presents with the classic triad of gait disturbance, incontinence, and cognitive changes, unlike spinal cord transection which causes motor level deficits.
